propositions: A single pending queue entry disables the O(1) fast-path gate marker store-wide, causing every subsequent write to pay a full directory walk (O(store)), costing ~1.2s at 4,938 tickets instead of 0.110ms
The marker is written only when a scan finds nothing, creating a binary trigger: even one pending entry clears it and forces full O(store) scans until the pending set empties

The marker is redesigned to record a live set of ticket ids with enqueued queue entries; a TTL-fresh marker with a non-empty live set scopes the walk to O(backlog) reductions instead of O(store), while the quiet fast path remains O(1)
Scoped probes do not rewrite the marker, preserving the TTL bound from the last full walk and maintaining the existing append-clears-marker race invariant

The scan loop including the f400 service-order (not_before_ns, id) sort is extracted into a shared _scan_pending helper so both full-walk and scoped-walk paths return identical ordering and service guarantees
Marker validation rejects wrong-typed live field (string or non-string list elements), degrading to full scan (preserving the existing three-rule honesty block comment for absence-only assertions)
